results.title: South Africa rethinks online gambling through strict digital enforcement and stronger consumer protection
results.content: The era of hands-off gambling regulation in South Africa is over. With the market generating R75 billion in gross gambling revenue on R1.5 trillion in total turnover, the stakes are too high for the status quo. In 2026, the national strategy is clear: regulate through digital platforms, not just around them. That means sharper legal definitions, enforceable digital controls, and consumer protection tools that reflect a market moving at the speed of technology.

results.title: No new taxes in 2027 Budget – Ampem Nyarko
results.content: Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Ampem Nyarko has hinted that no new taxes will be introduced in the 2027 Budget.

results.title: Six MDs in eight years weakened TOR – Managing Director
results.content: Frequent changes at the top of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) during the eight years of the previous administration undermined management stability and made it difficult to address the facility’s deep-rooted operational problems, the refinery’s Managing Director, Edmond Kombat, has said.

results.content: The Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko, has questioned how large quantities of cocaine continue to leave Ghana undetected following the seizure of 2.6 tonnes of the illicit drug by Spanish authorities.

results.title: Facing our past and shaping our future together – British High Commissioner to Ghana Dr. Christian Rogg writes
results.content: Britain and Ghana cannot change the past, but we can face it honestly, listen carefully and strengthen a modern partnership founded on dignity and mutual respect.

results.title: Industry, manufacturing must drive 2027 Budget — Awuah
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Association of Bankers, John Awuah, says lending to the private sector has increased by more than 30 per cent over the past year, but has challenged the government to use the 2027 Budget to stimulate demand for credit by supporting viable businesses and productive sectors.

results.title: AKSA bribery claims: Parliament finds no evidence against MPs, staff
results.content: Parliament has found no evidence that any Member of Parliament or officer of the Parliamentary Service received money allegedly paid to influence the approval of the 2015 AKSA emergency power agreement.

results.title: Police seize 3,752 slabs of suspected Indian hemp at Ada
results.content: The Tema Regional Police Command has intercepted a canoe carrying 3,752 slabs of suspected Indian hemp during an intelligence-led operation on the Volta Lake at Ada in the Greater Accra Region.

results.title: 120% collateral requirement shuts businesses out of credit — AGI
results.content: The Chairman of the Economic Affairs Committee of the Association of Ghana Industries (AGI), Eric Defor, has raised concerns about the difficulty businesses continue to face in securing bank loans, despite improved liquidity in the financial sector and a decline in interest rates.

results.title: ‘Buyers have no money; we are sitting idle’ — Kantamanto trader
results.content: Traders at the Kantamanto Market in Accra are struggling to make sales as customers increasingly complain about a lack of money to buy goods, a situation that is putting pressure on businesses and threatening their ability to remain profitable.

results.title: Stable prices, empty pockets: Kantamanto trader urges cash injection ahead of 2027 budget
results.content: A trader at the Kantamanto Market in Accra, Susana Asabea, has appealed to the government to take urgent steps to put more money in the hands of ordinary Ghanaians, saying the apparent stability in prices has yet to translate into improved business for traders.
